title: JavaScript string length in UTF-16 units
summary: Supplementary-plane characters typically take two UTF-16 code units. For example, "😀".length is 2.
detail: charCodeAt(0) gives only the high surrogate; codePointAt(0) returns the full code point for the character.
boundary: A grapheme cluster can be composed of multiple code points; traversing by code point is not guaranteed to equal the number of characters on the screen.
relevance: When mapping indices exported by the browser back into the original text, account for the extra code unit used by supplementary-plane characters.
